The chief architect of the Ottoman Empire for about fifty years, from 1538 until his death in 1588, under Suleiman the Magnificent and the two sultans after him. He is credited with more than 300 buildings and is the greatest architect of the Ottoman world.

He was born to a Christian family in central Anatolia and taken as a youth in the devshirme, the levy of boys for the sultan's service. He became a Muslim and served in the Janissaries as a military engineer, building bridges and ships on campaign, before he was made royal architect.

His works include mosques, colleges, hospitals, baths, bridges, aqueducts and inns across the empire, such as the Mehmed Paša Sokolović Bridge in Bosnia. His great aim was a central dome that filled the whole prayer hall with light. The Süleymaniye Mosque in Istanbul answered Hagia Sophia. He called the Selimiye Mosque in Edirne, finished in 1575, his masterpiece. His pupils built the Blue Mosque in Istanbul and helped spread his style.
